title: US forces disable Palau-flagged merchant ship trying to breach Iran port blockade in Gulf of Oman
summary: US Central Command said a US military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged merchant vessel Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on 26 November, disabling its propulsion after it left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas and tried to breach the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. CENTCOM said the civilian crew was unharmed. It is at least the 15th vessel publicly disclosed as disabled since the blockade began in the spring. On the same day Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a tanker using an unauthorised Strait of Hormuz route struck a naval mine.

reported_claims.text: A US military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday 26 November and its propulsion was ultimately disabled; the civilian crew was unharmed.
The Pacific Archer had left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas before attempting to breach the blockade; ship-tracking sites listed Singapore as its destination.
reported_claims.attributed_to: US officials and ship-tracking sites, as reported by the Associated Press

reported_claims.text: It is at least the 15th vessel publicly acknowledged as disabled since the blockade began, the sixth since it resumed in the summer, and the first since 7 November; the US says it has redirected 158 merchant ships since July.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Associated Press tally and US Central Command

reported_claims.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers tried to transit the Strait of Hormuz by an unauthorised route, that one struck a naval mine and the other turned back, and that such attempts had sharply decreased; the claims could not be independently verified.
Iranian navy commander Shahram Irani said on state television that Iran would carry out operations that would break the naval blockade and drive the enemy out of the region's waters.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Shahram Irani, Iranian navy commander (state TV)

unknowns: Identity, flag and fate of the tanker Iran says struck a mine, and whether the mine claim is true
Condition of the Pacific Archer and whether it is under tow or detained
Whether the two cited reports draw on the same AP copy beyond shared bylines
reassessment_triggers: Casualties from a blockade enforcement strike
Iranian naval action against US forces enforcing the blockade
Verified mine strikes on merchant ships in or near the Strait of Hormuz
impact_assessment: Potential: continued kinetic enforcement against merchant shipping raises risk to crews, insurance costs and the chance of direct US-Iran naval clashes; Iran's mine claim and threats point to a contested shipping lane.
priority_rationale: MODERATE: kinetic action against a merchant ship in an active blockade but no casualties and consistent with an established pattern; related to the wider Gulf conflict covered in GI-2026-0001.
monitoring_actions: Track CENTCOM statements on further disabled vessels
Watch UKMTO and IRGC reports of mine strikes or seizures
